We need to interpret the customer's message: "Not sure if I was even added to the sync." Likely they are a staff member not seeing SSO sign-in, suspect they aren't in sync. The policy excerpts cover why a staff member might not see SSO on sign-in, and how admin can check if account exists in Settings → People. The question: they are not sure if they were added to the sync. We can answer: explain that SSO appears only after sync creates account; admin can check in Settings → People; if not there, sync hasn't run yet; they may need to wait for next scheduled sync or admin to ensure account exists on identity provider side. We must answer using only policy excerpts. The answer should be short and specific. So we can say: The SSO sign‑in option only appears after the identity provider sync creates the account. If you don’t see it, you may be signing in before the next sync or the account isn’t on the IdP yet. An admin can verify in Settings → People; if the account isn’t listed, the sync hasn’t created it yet. They may need to wait for the next scheduled sync or have admin ensure the account exists on the IdP.

That aligns with DOC-010 parts. So we can post reply.

function.arguments: {"message":"The SSO sign‑in button only shows up after the identity‑provider sync has created your account. If you don’t see it, you may be signing in before the next scheduled sync runs, or your account hasn’t been created on the IdP side yet. An admin can confirm whether your account exists by going to **Settings → People** – SSO‑provisioned accounts are listed with the identity provider they came from. If you don’t appear there, the sync hasn’t created your account yet, so you’ll need to wait for the next sync or have an admin ensure the account exists in the IdP."}

arguments.message: The SSO sign‑in button only shows up after the identity‑provider sync has created your account. If you don’t see it, you may be signing in before the next scheduled sync runs, or your account hasn’t been created on the IdP side yet. An admin can confirm whether your account exists by going to **Settings → People** – SSO‑provisioned accounts are listed with the identity provider they came from. If you don’t appear there, the sync hasn’t created your account yet, so you’ll need to wait for the next sync or have an admin ensure the account exists in the IdP.
